name: Priya Zhang

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This is confidential. What does your normal workday look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and manage nine people who set prices for replacement parts at a large appliance company. We compare costs, check margins and answer the sales desks when a price makes no sense. I’ve managed the team for six years and do the job about as well as the other managers. I use AI every day to find odd price changes, but I still ask a buyer why a part costs what it does.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is happening at home, and how much financial room do you have?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband, Amir, maintains school buildings, and our children are eight and fourteen. We have a mortgage, my pay is high for this role and we have about thirteen months of expenses saved, plus retirement savings we do not want to touch. There are plenty of similar offices nearby. I have a bachelor’s degree, like testing tools early and still think a paid apprenticeship can teach more than a course with no real work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the sales desks to keep asking why a price looks wrong. A tool that finds an odd number is useful, but someone still has to check the supplier cost.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My job should be fine, and thirteen months saved means a bad quarter would not force us to move. I would be pleased if the routine price file took less time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I’d keep the Monday price review and use AI to flag unusual changes before a buyer checks the cost record. In the first year Amir and I would keep investing 300 a month in a broad retirement fund only after mortgage and our cash reserve are covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm. I could spend more time with the team on prices that actually confuse customers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is the last odd price you caught?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A small gasket was listed above the cost of a whole pump. The buyer found a bad supplier code before the sales desk quoted it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why invest only after the cash reserve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A fund can fall in value when we need money. I want the mortgage and a year of bills in cash first.

say: I’d tell sales desks to ask why a **part price looks wrong** before quoting it to customers.
AI flags still need **supplier-cost checks** against the record.
think: My **pricing job** looks secure in a plateau.
Thirteen months saved protect us from a **bad quarter**.
I would enjoy less **routine price-file work** each week.
do: Keep **Monday price reviews** with buyer checks of AI flags.
Invest **300 monthly** in a broad retirement fund only after mortgage and one year’s bills remain in cash.
feel: I feel **calm** about work and household cash.
S0.quote: A small gasket was listed above the cost of a whole pump.
fieldNote: She uses **AI every day** to flag price errors.
High pay and **thirteen months saved** cushion a bad quarter.
She invests only after **cash and mortgage** obligations are covered.

steps.text: Keep Monday price reviews and check AI flags against supplier costs
Invest 300 monthly in broad retirement fund only after mortgage and one-year cash reserve hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say buying, checking and answering sales questions are exposed now, so we should test automation on real price errors. I’d show the team how many manual checks remain before changing their posts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the price file writes itself, the company could run two categories under one manager. I use AI early, but my own role could still be reduced to a part-time check.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This quarter I’d bring in an AI checker for one product category only after the finance director approves a six-week trial, and I’d compare it with two hundred old price changes. In the first year I’d learn the audit controls on paid company time and ask for a written role if the team is merged, while keeping the cash reserve untouched.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious about losing hours, though I like improving the file. A clever price checker is not a promise of my salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who sees the errors in that trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The buyers and sales desk should see each wrong margin before it reaches a customer. I would put the false alerts and missed errors on the same page.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you launch it without the finance director?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. My team cannot change live prices on my enthusiasm alone; the director must approve the trial and its limits.

say: I’d test **real price errors** before using the checker on live sales prices.
Staff should see the **remaining manual checks** before their posts change.
think: One manager could cover **two product categories** once the price file writes itself.
Using AI every day does not guarantee **full-time hours** for me.
do: Run a **six-week checker trial** only with finance approval.
Learn **audit controls** on paid time and request a written role if teams merge.
S1.quote: A clever price checker is not a promise of my salary.
fieldNote: She pilots automation only with **director approval**.
The trial compares **two hundred old prices**, not live guesses.
She separates tool improvement from **her own job security**.

steps.text: Trial AI price checking for six weeks only after finance director approval
Compare the checker against two hundred old price changes
Learn pricing audit controls during paid company hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the company for written job dates, severance and someone responsible for a wrong part price. I would tell the sales desks to keep copies of the cost record.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could set and explain prices better and cheaper than my whole team, so I expect my manager post to go. Amir’s school maintenance is hands-on until robots arrive around 2031, and his wage plus our thirteen-month reserve give us room to choose, though we cannot live forever on one paycheck.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week Amir and I would cancel the planned home extension and keep its deposit in cash. Before 2028 I’d ask for a written severance figure and compare real posted jobs at nearby firms, knowing their pricing desks face the same AGI; in the first year after AGI, I’d apply only for a time-limited paid role if its wage covers my share of the mortgage and the work is actually posted.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m alarmed about losing a high income, even with savings. I would be awake thinking about how long Amir’s maintenance work would last after 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why a time-limited role if other desks face AGI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A paid bridge buys another month without spending the reserve. I would not call another pricing title protection from 2028 AGI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you invest more money during that search?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I’d hold the cash reserve and pause new fund contributions until we know whether another wage arrives.

say: I’d ask for job dates and **written severance** before the pricing team changes.
Sales desks need a **responsible price contact** when a part costs the wrong amount.
think: I **expect my pricing post** to end in 2028.
Amir’s **hands-on wage** may last until 2031 robots; thirteen months saved gives us some room to choose.
do: Cancel the **home extension** and keep its deposit in cash.
Compare **posted paid bridges** and apply only with written mortgage-share wages after 2028.
Pause **new fund contributions** after AGI until another wage is secured.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about our high-wage loss.
S2.quote: I would not call another pricing title protection from 2028 AGI.
fieldNote: She expects the **2028 thinking system** to remove pricing management.
Nearby desk roles are **temporary bridges**, not safe substitutes.
She pauses new investments while protecting **cash for bills**.

steps.text: Cancel the planned home extension and retain its deposit in cash
Compare actual posted time-limited roles at nearby firms before 2028
Apply for posted paid bridge work after 2028 only if wages cover her mortgage share

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say five years gives workers and employers time to show real vacancies and written pay instead of selling a short course. I’d want a named person checking customer prices until the change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could use five years to reduce the mortgage while my salary continues. A role checking prices at another company still faces AGI in 2031; Amir’s physical school maintenance faces robots around 2034, so we need to keep cash available.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January 2027 Amir and I would put an extra 350 monthly against the mortgage only while our thirteen-month cash reserve remains intact. I’d keep the pricing role, review posted jobs every quarter and take a short paid bridge role before 2031 only if its written wage covers my mortgage share; in the first year after AGI, I’d use the reserve while searching if no paid post remains.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious but can plan with a real balance sheet. Five years gives us time to reduce fixed bills without claiming I can out-prompt AGI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you buy a course to change fields?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if an employer offered paid work with it. I would not spend the reserve on a certificate whose wage nobody can name.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say we are paying down the house so their choices do not depend on one office salary. I would not pick an apprenticeship for them, but I would show them real wage adverts.

say: I’d demand **real vacancies and wages** before anyone buys a course.
Customer prices need a **named checker** while the team changes.
think: I could reduce the **mortgage** while my salary continues before 2031.
Another pricing desk still faces **2031 AGI**.
Amir’s physical maintenance faces **2034 robots**, so our cash matters.
do: Overpay the **mortgage by 350** only while thirteen months of cash remain.
Review **posted jobs quarterly** and take a bridge only at written mortgage-share pay.
Use the **cash reserve** to search after 2031 if no paid post remains.
feel: I feel **anxious** but able to plan.
S3.quote: I would not spend the reserve on a certificate whose wage nobody can name.
fieldNote: She pays debt only while **cash reserves** remain intact.
She rejects a **course** without a paid job.
The family has **2031 desk risk** and later 2034 maintenance robots.

steps.text: Pay 350 extra monthly on mortgage only while thirteen months of cash remain
Review posted paid roles at nearby firms each quarter
Take a short paid bridge before 2031 only if written wages cover mortgage share

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say ten years lets a company publish the end of pricing jobs and the pay for any replacement work. Families can plan when the dates and wages are real.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 53 in 2036, with both children grown. If Amir and I keep earning, we might finish the mortgage and keep a year in cash. My pricing work and any other office bridge still face 2036 AGI, while his physical maintenance faces robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January 2027 I’d raise mortgage overpayments to 450 monthly only if the thirteen-month cash reserve stays untouched and Amir’s wage holds. I’d invest 200 monthly in a broad fund only after those conditions are met and keep checking real local vacancies; in the first year after AGI, I’d stop new investments if either job ended and use cash for a search rather than pretend an office title is safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy rather than trapped. A decade can turn a high wage into a smaller mortgage, provided we do not spend the reserve to look rich.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you quit now to invest full-time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I want the wage while the firm pays it, and a broad fund can fall when we need cash.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to your older child about careers?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell them to look at paid apprenticeships and actual openings alongside degrees. I would not choose my older child’s career path, but I would show the wage numbers.

say: I’d ask for **job end dates** and written wages on replacement roles.
Real figures give families **time to plan** before incomes change.
think: We might finish the **mortgage** if both wages hold.
Every office bridge faces **2036 AGI** before 2039 maintenance robots.
do: Overpay **450 monthly** only with cash reserve and Amir’s wage intact.
Invest **200 monthly** only after those conditions, and pause contributions if either job ends.
Check **real local vacancies** before 2036 and use cash for a search after AGI if jobs end.
feel: I feel **uneasy** but able to reduce debt.
S4.quote: I would not choose my older child’s career path, but I would show the wage numbers.
fieldNote: She conditions investment on **cash reserves** and mortgage cover.
She treats another office role as a **paid bridge** only.
She supports her child’s choice with **wage adverts** rather than choosing for them.

steps.text: Pay 450 extra monthly on mortgage only if thirteen-month reserve and Amir’s wage hold
Invest 200 monthly only after mortgage overpayment cash reserve and Amir’s wage are covered
Check real local job postings before 2036 for paid roles with written wages

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because a whole pricing team could disappear while Amir’s maintenance job has its own later robot date. Written severance, a clear pay figure on any real opening and time to keep our cash reserve would help. I can learn tools quickly, but I cannot make an exposed office role safe by using them.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who pays when a part price is wrong and a family repairs a broken fridge. A low price on a screen does not replace the part in a warm kitchen.

headlineQuote: A low price on a screen does not replace the part in a warm kitchen.
portrait: **Priya**, 43, is an experienced parts-pricing manager with a bachelor’s degree.
High pay and **thirteen months saved** support a mortgage and two school-age children.
She uses **AI daily** and trials pricing automation with finance approval.
She keeps **cash ahead of investing** while treating nearby desk posts as paid bridges.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her pricing post before the household adjusts to one wage.
whatWouldHelp: **Written severance**, wages on real openings and time to preserve cash would help.
